title: Clean Call Halts Under the Release Wrapper
statement: Let $C$ be a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine, with entry and exit states, and let $x$, $arg$, $result$, and $out$ be Boolean words. Suppose a call from the seam configuration with entry state and tape word $arg$ reaches the seam configuration with exit state and tape word $result$, emitting exactly $out$, after a positive number $t$ of steps. Suppose also that its state is not the exit state at any time strictly between $0$ and $t$. Then the release wrapper, started with its release flag false at the entry seam, reaches after $t+1$ steps a halted configuration with release flag true, exit state, tape word $result$, and output $out$.
hypotheses_covered: $C$ is a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine, with states $entry$ and $exit$
The underlying run reaches the specified exit seam and output at time $t$
The underlying run's state differs from $exit$ at each time $v$ with $0<v<t$
replaced: Suppose a clean call runs from its entry over an argument word to its exit over a result word with some emitted output, in positive time $t$, never showing the exit strictly between $0$ and $t$. Then the release wrapper, started unreleased at the entry, halts physically at time $t + 1$ with exactly the result's canonical seam, the same emitted output, and no further transition.
